grants.title: GO8341: Modernised Multicultural Grants Program: Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be divided into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for each batch: Batch 1 - closes 4:00 pm AEST on 18 May 2026 - ID 2025-5201 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 4:00 pm AEDT on 12 November 2026 - ID 2026-6462 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting organisations through an open competitive process to apply to deliver community infrastructure under the Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities program from 2026–27. The Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities grant opportunity provides total funding of up to $41.6 million (GST exclusive) for construction, upgrade or extension of infrastructure. You can apply for one of 3 streams of grant funding based on the type of infrastructure project and amount of grant funding you require for the project. The grant opportunity is comprised of 2 funding opportunities, called batches. You can apply for funding in one batch. Batch 1 opens on 7 April 2026 and closes on 18 May 2026. Batch 2 opens on 18 May 2026 and closes on 12 November 2026. The following groups and projects will be prioritised for funding: new and emerging multicultural communities, as defined below projects focussed on achieving positive outcomes for multicultural women, multicultural LGBTIQA+ community members, and multicultural people with a disability. Co-contributions are required towards the value of your project and the minimum amount of co funding is determined by whether you are applying as a priority group/project or other. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to: deliver physical infrastructure to support multicultural communities connect and commune in a designated physical environment provide co-funding to deliver community-focussed infrastructure and amenities provide infrastructure and amenities that benefit the wider multicultural community by improving equity and social inclusion.

grants.title: GO8220: Saluting their Service Commemorative Grants Program 2026–27
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for all 2 batches: Batch 1 - closes 9:00 PM AEST on 29 July 2026 - ID 2025-5415 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 9:00 PM AEDT 21 January 2027 - ID 2025-5416 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting eligible organisations to apply for grant funding under the Saluting Their Service Commemorative Grants Program (STS program). The objective of the STS Program is to commemorate the service and sacrifice of Australia’s service personnel who served in wars, conflicts and peace operations, including National Service personnel, and their families. The intended outcome of the STS Program is to provide funding for projects and activities that: promote appreciation and understanding of the experiences of service, and the role of service personnel preserve, add to the sum of knowledge on, or provide access to information about Australia’s wartime heritage. 1. Community Grants Grants up to $10,000 are available for projects and activities that: are focused on the local community commemorate the service and sacrifice of local community members are primarily accessed by the local community. 2. Major Grants Grants between $10,001 and $150,000 are available for major commemorative projects and activities that are significant from a national, state, territory and/or broader regional perspective. These projects may include the construction of new war or peace memorials where none currently exist, as well as additions to existing memorials. If your project relates to restoring or changing a memorial or other commemorative artefact, there may be heritage and conservation considerations.

grants.title: GO8521: Carer Peak Body Organisational Support and National Carers Week
grants.summary: The Carers Peak Body Organisation Support and National Carers Week programs (the programs) will run over 5 years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. The program is a continuation of the Carer Peak Bodies and National Carers Week program (2019-25). It provides organisation support for peak representation of carers and their interests as representatives. The program would receive funding of $4,725,000 (indexed) to continue to provide organisation support for peak representation of carers and their interests as representatives into 2030-31. The purpose of this grant opportunity is twofold: to represent the Australian Government as the National Carers Peak Body and to deliver on the objectives of both the Carers Peak Body Organisation Support and National Carers Week programs. Expected outcomes include improved policies and services, greater recognition of carers, increased community awareness, stronger engagement, and better access to supports. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8520: Carer Inclusive Workplace Initiative
grants.summary: The Carer Inclusive Workplace Initiative Program (the program) will run over 2 years from 2026-27 to 2027-28. This grant program supports the Australian Government’s contribution to outcomes for Disability and Carers by advancing the objectives of Program 4.1 - Disability and Carers. The objective of the grant opportunity is to assist and encourage employers to develop and adopt practices that encourages and support employees with caring responsibilities. The purpose of this grant opportunity is to expand carer inclusivity in workplaces around Australia. It will enable businesses, in particular small businesses, to self-identify as a carer inclusive organisation without the time commitment and cost associated with a full accreditation process. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8511: Round 3 – Closing the Gap – Major Capital Works Program – 2026-27
grants.summary: For this grant opportunity, up to $180 million is available over two years (2026–27 to 2027–28). The funding aims to strengthen the Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Service (ACCHS) sector through improved infrastructure, including new and upgraded health clinics and associated housing for health professionals. Two funding rounds totalling $210 million have already been delivered under the Closing the Gap Major Capital Works (MCW) Program (Round 1 through GO5504 and Round 2 through GO6522). The current round represents Round 3 of the Closing the Gap MCW Program. Note: Please refer to updated Grant Opportunity Guidelines - Version 2 - published on 24 August 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8562: Community Controlled Transition Care (CCTC)
grants.summary: The Indigenous Australians’ Health Programme (IAHP) aims to increase access to culturally appropriate and self-determined health care by prioritising Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services (ACCHSs) to lead the delivery of programs and services. This grant opportunity’s purpose is to provide the National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation (NACCHO) with funding to deliver the Community Controlled Transition Care (CCTC) program. The CCTC program will involve the co-design and delivery of a community controlled transition care model for First Nations peoples exiting custody. It will seek to improve health care access and outcomes for First Nations people in the custodial system, providing First Nations peoples with improved discharge planning, reintegration support and culturally safe health care post-release. The Australian Government has announced a total of $14,497,810 over 3 years for the CCTC grant opportunity. The grant opportunity will run from November 2026 to June 2029. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8527: WA Roadmap Implementation Fund: Farm System Productivity Program
grants.summary: The program was announced as part of the $5.0 million WA Roadmap Implementation Fund in support of the recommendations in the WA Sheep Industry Roadmap to 2028 (the Roadmap)(www.thefutureflock.com.au/wa-roadmap-to-2028). The Roadmap sets out a forward-looking plan to guide Western Australia’s (WA) sheep industry transition away from live sheep exports by sea. Developed by industry and informed by extensive consultation, it identifies key challenges and opportunities and outlines a clear, practical path for growth, innovation and sustainability. The Roadmap outlines strategies and initiatives to address these challenges and opportunities, guiding future development, investment and collaboration. The program targets opportunities identified in the Roadmap and supports projects that are aligned with the strategies and initiatives identified in the Roadmap against the three goals: The whole supply chain operating efficiently to optimise market value and profitability Informed, confident decision-making across the industry A vibrant, positive and collaborative industry culture The program will consider a broad range of project proposals from the not-for-profit and commercial sectors to improve productivity, profitability and industry collaboration in implementing the Roadmap. Successful project proposals will demonstrate benefit to the broader WA sheep industry. The objective of this grant opportunity is: To assist sheep producers affected by the phase out of live sheep exports by sea by supporting projects that will enhanceon-farm systems and productivity, improve whole of supply chain profitability, and support a more collaborative industry culture. The intended outcome of this grant opportunity is: To improve confidence and productivity in farm systems as sheep producers adjust to changing markets and transition away from live sheep exports by sea.

grants.title: GO8560: Indigenous Broadcasting and Media Program – Strengthening Community Broadcasting Grant Opportunity
grants.summary: The Indigenous Broadcasting and Media Program – Strengthening Community Broadcasting Grant Opportunity will provide grant funding of up to $4 million (GST exclusive) for grant activities to eligible applicants to strengthen the First Nations community broadcasting sector. Program objectives include supporting the First Nations broadcasting and media sector to modernise and stabilise operations and supporting the First Nations broadcasting and media sector to deliver reliable, high quality, culturally and locally relevant broadcasting services. The intended outcomes of the grant are: Improved capacity of First Nations broadcasting and media services to deliver high quality broadcasting services. Relevant First Nations news, information, cultural and educational programs remain accessible. Opportunities for training and development in the First Nations Broadcasting and Media sector are provided. Increase in the number of First Nations community broadcasting services operating in Australia.

grants.title: GO8551: WA Roadmap Implementation Fund: Training Capability and Farm Systems Program
grants.summary: The program was announced as part of the $5.0 million WA Roadmap Implementation Fund in support of the recommendations in the WA Sheep Industry Roadmap to 2028 (the Roadmap)(www.thefutureflock.com.au/wa-roadmap-to-2028). The Roadmap sets out a forward-looking plan to guide Western Australia’s (WA) sheep industry transition away from live sheep exports by sea. Developed by industry and informed by extensive consultation, it identifies key challenges and opportunities and outlines a clear, practical path for growth, innovation and sustainability. The Roadmap outlines strategies and initiatives to address these challenges and opportunities, guiding future development, investment and collaboration. The program targets opportunities identified in the Roadmap and supports projects that are aligned with the strategies and initiatives identified in the Roadmap against the three goals: The whole supply chain operating efficiently to optimise market value and profitability Informed, confident decision-making across the industry A vibrant, positive and collaborative industry culture This program support projects that help improve productivity and build capability across WA’s sheep industry. Projects should align with the opportunities identified in the WA Roadmap to 2028 and may include activities including but not limited to train-the-trainer programs, peer-to-peer training for producers and supply chain participants, leadership development, demonstration sites, and relevant equipment needed to support those activities. The objective of the program is: To assist sheep producers affected by the phase out of live sheep exports by sea to improve their capability, productivity and sustainability. The intended outcomes of the program are: Increased confidence and productivity in farm systems as sheep producers adapt to changing markets and transition away from live sheep exports by sea.

grants.title: GO8232: MRFF – Clinical Trials Activity Initiative – 2026 International Clinical Trial Collaborations Grant Opportunity
grants.summary: The Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) Clinical Trials Activity Initiative (the Initiative) aims to increase clinical trial activity in Australia in order to improve the evidence base supporting clinical care and to help patients access trials relevant to their health circumstances and enable researchers to bring international trials to Australian patients. The objective of this grant opportunity is to provide grants of financial assistance to support medical research and medical innovation projects that: Promote Australian involvement in international collaborative investigator-initiated clinical trials research through the establishment and co-ordination of clinical trial site/s in Australia. Provide high-quality evidence of the effectiveness of novel health treatments, drugs or devices in ‘usual care’ settings, which will support a decision on whether to deliver the intervention in an Australian setting. The intended outcome of the research is to improve the health and wellbeing of Australians by investing in new clinical trials that support increased access to high-quality, evidence-based and effective health care. Applicants to this grant opportunity must propose a clinical trial in Australia in collaboration with international counterparts. The clinical trial should not have commenced recruitment at the Australian trial site/s. Please note the 2026 MRFF International Clinical Trial Collaborations grant opportunity will be open for one round only. This grant opportunity is being administered by NHMRC on behalf of the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. Further information on the Medical Research Future Fund is available from the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing's website. A list of Eligible Organisations can be found on the NHMRC List of MRFF Eligible Organisations webpage

grants.title: GO8494: Regional, Rural and Remote Capacity Building grant opportunity 2026
grants.summary: The objectives of this grant opportunity are to provide financial assistance to support: •established regional, rural or remote (RRR) researchers, as they lead and develop a team of early to mid-career RRR researchers to build RRR research capacity •emerging RRR researchers, including clinician researchers, to be future research leaders in their communities •place-based research conducted in RRR areas that aims to benefit individuals and communities living in those areas. The intended outcomes of this grant opportunity are to: •build capacity in the RRR research workforce across Australia, including clinician researchers •strengthen health and medical research in RRR communities to improve health equity. Funding will be available under 2 application streams: •Stream 1: the Chief Investigators are primarily resident in a regional, rural, remote or very remote area according to the Modified Monash Model (MM 2–7). •Stream 2: the Chief Investigators are primarily resident in a rural, remote or very remote area according to the Modified Monash Model (MM 3–7). The applicant team may be based at a single institution, organisation or campus in one RRR region or may be a geographically disparate network linking across more than one RRR region. Applications that include at least one health service provider and clinician researcher are encouraged. Applications that address health services and programs to improve health outcomes for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people are also encouraged. Grants are to support a program of research that may consist of multiple smaller-scale research projects. Grantees will have the flexibility to pursue important new research directions as they arise, adjust their resources accordingly, and to form collaborations as needed.

grants.title: GO8555: COALAR Grant Round 2026-27
grants.summary: The Council on Australia Latin America Relations (COALAR) Grant Program is an annual grant program offering funding to organisations and individuals to support projects or activities which advance Australia's engagement with Latin America, including exchanges, partnerships and other collaborations aligned with COALAR’s strategic priority areas and goals. COALAR’s Strategic Priority Areas are: 1 - Culture and Entrepreneurship; 2 - Education and Research; 3 - Environment and Energy Transition; 4 - First Nations; and 5 - Mining, Mining Equipment, Technology and Services (METS), and Resources. COALAR’s Strategic Goals are: Goal 1 - Raise awareness of COALAR and Latin America-Australia relations; Goal 2 - Strengthen commercial ties; Goal 3 - Expand social and cultural connections; and Goal 4 -Foster and promote gender equality and women’s leadership. Applications will be prioritised for projects taking place in the following countries: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, México, Panamá, Perú and Uruguay. Grants between $15,000 to $50,000, from a total funding pool of up to $300,000, is available to support projects for a maximum of 12 months. Grant projects must commence no earlier than 1 March 2027 and before 30 June 2027. The grant round will be conducted in a one-stage full application process.

grants.title: GO8439: Defence Strategic Policy Research Program
grants.summary: The Defence Strategic Policy Research Program grant opportunity will provide operating funding to the Australian strategic policy sector for up to five years, from 2027–28 to 2031–32. This grant opportunity was established to implement the government response to the 2024 Independent Review of Commonwealth funding for strategic policy work (the Varghese review). The grant opportunity is confined to activities that support the Australian Defence Force (or other defence purposes), with the majority of an organisation’s business-as-usual activities directed toward the annual national security policy research priorities, set by the Secretaries’ Committee on National Security (SCNS) and published by the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to promote the development of Australia’s defence and national security policy and strategy by: informing and shaping debate through quality research, discussion fora, and other strategic policy work on Australian strategic and defence policy issues deepening public discussion on Australia’s strategic and defence policy choices strengthening engagement between Defence and the strategic policy sector. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: published original, evidence-based strategic policy research development of new and emerging talent within the Australian strategic policy sector, promoting equitable and diverse participation, including with gender-diverse and/or First Nations-led organisations enhanced engagement with public and private sector experts, including outside metropolitan locations enriched professional development for Defence personnel (military and civilian).

grants.title: GO8455: Integrated Carer Support Service: Carer Gateway Service Providers (CGSPs)
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to select a network of providers to deliver supports and services for unpaid carers across 19 Carer Gateway service areas. Only one provider will be selected per service area, however providers may apply for, and be selected for multiple service areas. Services offered include support planning, counselling, coaching, training, peer support, tailored support packages, referrals to access planned and emergency respite, navigation assistance with mainstream services and information and advice. Services will be prioritised and delivered, based on the needs of carers. Successful providers must deliver all the service types listed, however there is flexibility in delivery models and how much funding is applied to each service. Providers will monitor demand in the service area and configure services and allocate resources to maximise outcomes based on to carers’ needs within the service area. It is expected that service delivery will change over time in response to changes in demand, and as new support options and approaches emerge. Providers are to establish and maintain outreach activities, and link to social, health, education, community and cultural groups, to better understand carer cohorts in the service area, including (but not limited to) those in regional, rural and remote locations and the specific carer cohorts identified in the National Carer Strategy 2024-2034 and National Carer Strategy Action Plan 2024-2027. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8554: Continuation of viral hepatitis prevention and response measures
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to provide funding to support organisations in the design and delivery of national viral hepatitis community-led initiatives and awareness raising campaigns that engage priority populations, including people at higher risk of acquiring viral hepatitis or with limited access to health care. These activities will help reduce stigma and encourage individuals to seek care and reduce hepatitis-related cancer mortality. This includes: • $6.9 million from 1 January 2027 to 30 June 2029 for National Hepatitis B projects. • $9.0 million 1 January 2027 to 30 June 2029 for National Hepatitis C projects. The objectives of the grant are: • To provide funding to eligible organisations to maintain nationally coordinated activities that improve prevention, testing, diagnosis and treatment outcomes for hepatitis B and C. • To provide funding to eligible organisations to deliver evidence-based activities that address gaps in hepatitis B and C continuum of care. • To address goals and targets in the Strategies. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: • To support harm reduction, public awareness and education, and targeted approaches that increase testing, reduce stigma and discrimination, and strengthen access to culturally safe and appropriate care, particularly among priority populations experiencing inequitable health outcomes. • To reduce hepatitis-related cancer mortality. • To support the national elimination of hepatitis B and C as public health challenges in Australia by 2030. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO7926: General Practice Incentive Fund
grants.summary: The Primary Health Networks (PHN) Program General Practice Incentive Fund (GPIF) grant opportunity (the grant opportunity) will enable the design and implementation of health care services in communities where primary care and related service systems: fail are at imminent risk of failure, or are characterised by ongoing instability. The department will identify intervention sites for where the grant opportunity may be targeted. Once a site is identified, the Decision Maker will agree for the relevant PHN to be invited to the grant opportunity. The site identification process includes consultation with relevant jurisdictions (state and territory governments). It will consider information available to the department regarding community impact of service instability or failure. The PHN and/or Rural Workforce Agency (RWA) specific to the identified site may also be consulted to understand local issues. Phase 1: Planning/co-design PHN undertakes consultation with relevant stakeholders for planning and co-design of a service system recovery plan (SSRP). Phase 2: Implementation Implement and evaluate approved SSRP activities. Funding for implementation activities will be determined through assessment of applications (i.e. SSRPs submitted according to the Application Form). Note: Please refer to the most recent version of the Attachment Pack (Implementation Plan, Engagement Strategy, Budget and Risk Management Plan) published on 4 December 2025. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8518: First Nations Clean Energy Projects – Pilot Grants
grants.summary: The First Nations Clean Energy Projects – Pilot Grants provides funding to First Nations organisations. This program was announced as part of the implementation of the Government’s First Nations Clean Energy Strategy. The objectives of the program are to: support up to 2 First Nations organisations to progress their clean energy projects beyond feasibility towards financial close build evidence of the factors that enable increased investment in First Nations clean energy projects share First Nations clean energy project development lessons learnt with the sector. The intended outcome of the program is to support the economic development and self-determination of First Nations peoples through increased opportunities to lead and benefit from clean energy project developments. There is a total of up to $10 million available for this grant program. Grants will be from $1 million to $10 million. The grant amount will be up to 100% of eligible expenditure.

grants.title: GO8507: Dementia Training Program
grants.summary: The Dementia Training Program (DTP), first established nationally in 2016, aims to strengthen the capability of Australia’s health and aged care workforce to provide high-quality, evidence-based dementia care. The purpose of this grant opportunity is to fund the delivery of accredited and non-accredited education, upskilling and professional development in dementia care. The delivery of DTP activities will reflect the emerging dementia, health and aged care landscape, including recent aged care reforms and increasing demand for services. DTP activities will: • Be aligned with a National Dementia Training and Education Standards Framework. • Expand experiential, immersive, peer mentoring and interprofessional training. • Adopt tailored approaches for diverse workforce groups and communities including for First Nations people, those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and people from regional, rural and remote locations. • Build organisational capability and leadership for high quality dementia care, including sustainable practice change. • Deliver key service elements responding to the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety. There are two funding streams: Stream 1 aims to improve capability of health and aged care workers to provide high quality dementia care for non-Indigenous Australians, including people from diverse backgrounds. Stream 2 focuses on culturally safe, community-led dementia training for First Nations communities and workforces. NOTE: Please refer to the most recent Frequently Asked Questions (Version 3) published 20 August 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.
